title: Mapping Insertion Sites of Tol2 Transgenes in Zebrafish Using TransTag
author: Wei, Naidu, et al.
materials: NEBNext High Fidelity 2× PCR Master Mix

steps.title: Prepare adapters and primers
steps.instruction: Resuspend ME adapters B and Reverse oligonucleotides to 100 µM in ddH₂O and store at –20 °C; dilute i5 and i7 primers to 100 µM stock, make 10 µM working aliquots and store at –20 °C. All steps must be performed under DNase‑free conditions.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend each ME adapter B and Reverse oligo in ddH₂O to a final concentration of 100 µM.
Aliquot and store the resuspended adapters at –20 °C.
Dilute i5 and i7 primers to 100 µM stock in ddH₂O.
Prepare 10 µM working solutions of i5 and i7 primers, aliquot, and store at –20 °C.

steps.title: Extract and clean genomic DNA
steps.instruction: Lyse zebrafish tissue with alkaline buffer, neutralize, spin down, and purify DNA using a Zymo DNA Clean & Concentrator kit; elute in 25 µL ddH₂O, quantify with NanoDrop, and store at –20 °C if not used immediately.

substeps.instruction: Transfer zebrafish tissue (fin clip, embryo, or larvae) to a clean PCR tube.
Add 50 µL alkaline lysis buffer, ensure tissue is fully submerged, and incubate 30 min at 95 °C in a thermal cycler.
Vortex 3–5 s, add 50 µL neutralization buffer, and mix by pipetting.
Spin 3–5 s in a bench‑top microcentrifuge; transfer the supernatant (genomic DNA) to a new tube.
Clean up the DNA with a Zymo Research DNA Clean & Concentrator kit (or equivalent) following the manufacturer’s protocol.
Elute the purified DNA in 25 µL ddH₂O.
Measure DNA concentration with a NanoDrop spectrophotometer (optional agarose gel check for quality).
Store the DNA at –20 °C for up to several weeks before library preparation.

steps.title: First-round PCR amplification
steps.instruction: Set up a 25 µL PCR on ice using ME‑A‑Tol2 and i7 primers with NEBNext 2× HiFi Master Mix and tagmented DNA, then run the specified thermocycling program.

substeps.instruction: In a PCR tube on ice, combine 12.5 µL NEBNext 2× HiFi Master Mix, 10.5 µL tagmented DNA, 1 µL i7 primer (10 µM), and 1 µL ME‑A‑Tol2 primer (10 µM).
Thermocycler program:
• 72 °C for 5 min (gap filling)
• 98 °C for 30 s (initial denaturation)
• 98 °C for 10 s (denaturation) – 20 cycles
• 63 °C for 15 s (extension/elongation)
• 72 °C for 60 s (final extension)
• Hold at 4 °C.
If multiplexing, use a uniquely barcoded i7 primer for each sample and record the barcode for downstream demultiplexing.

steps.title: Second-round PCR amplification
steps.instruction: Using the first‑round product, set up a second 25 µL PCR with i5 and i7 primers and run the second‑round thermocycling program, keeping the same i7 primer as in round one.

substeps.instruction: In a new PCR tube on ice, combine 25 µL NEBNext 2× HiFi Master Mix, 12.5 µL first‑round PCR product, 2 µL i5 primer (10 µM), 2 µL i7 primer (10 µM, same as round one), and 8.5 µL ddH₂O.
Thermocycler program:
• 98 °C for 30 s (initial denaturation)
• 98 °C for 10 s (denaturation) – 20 cycles
• 63 °C for 15 s (extension/elongation)
• 72 °C for 60 s (final extension)
• Hold at 4 °C.
Record the unique i5/i7 primer pair used for each library for later demultiplexing.

steps.title: Clean up PCR product and quantify
steps.instruction: Purify the second‑round PCR using AMPure XP beads, elute in ddH₂O, quantify with Qubit, and store the final library at –20 °C; typical concentration is ~20 ng/µL and libraries are ready for 150 bp sequencing (1–5 M reads per sample).

substeps.instruction: Add 55 µL (1.1× the sample volume) AMPure XP beads to each 25 µL PCR reaction.
Incubate as per bead protocol, place on magnetic rack, wash beads, and elute the DNA in 15 µL ddH₂O.
Transfer the eluate to a new PCR tube and measure concentration with a Qubit fluorometer.
The resulting library can be quality‑controlled (Bioanalyzer/TapeStation) and stored at –20 °C.
Typical final library concentration: ~20 ng/µL.
Recommended sequencing: 150 bp reads, 1–5 million reads per sample.

steps.title: Analyze data with Shiny app
steps.instruction: Upload the raw R1 FASTQ file to the TransTag Shiny web app, adjust read‑length cutoff quantile, review the top 15 genomic regions, blast flanking sequences to the zebrafish genome, and validate insertion sites by locus‑specific PCR.

substeps.instruction: Open https://menglab.shinyapps.io/transtag_alignmentfree/ in a web browser.
Upload the first‑read (R1) FASTQ file (must be < 1 GB; for larger files run the local R script from https://github.com/fanjumeng/TransTag).
Set the read‑length cutoff quantile between 0.2 and 0.9 (default 0.75) as desired.
Examine the displayed top 15 most frequent genomic regions and their read counts.
Copy the flanking genomic sequences and BLAST them against the zebrafish genome (e.g., UCSC BLAT) to obtain insertion coordinates.
Design locus‑specific PCR primers flanking the identified insertion site and perform PCR validation.
